chapter_meta.description: Black builds the solid c6-d5-e6 pawn triangle. White completes development and prepares the central break e2-e4 to free the g2-bishop on the long diagonal.

main.explanation: White occupies the center with the queen's pawn and gains a first foothold for the central pawns.
main.hint: Start by claiming the center with a pawn.

main.strategic_idea: Stop White from occupying e4 with a pawn.
main.explanation: Black develops flexibly and controls e4, so White cannot easily build a full pawn center with e2-e4.

main.strategic_idea: Attack the d5 square and open lines for the queenside pieces.
main.explanation: The c-pawn fights for d5 and makes room for White's queenside pieces to develop.
main.hint: Use your c-pawn to fight for d5.

main.strategic_idea: Support the center and open a path for the dark-squared bishop.
main.explanation: Black prepares ...d5 and opens the f8-bishop's diagonal toward e7, d6 or b4.

main.strategic_idea: Prepare the fianchetto of the king's bishop.
main.explanation: White makes room on g2 for the light-squared bishop, which will aim down the long diagonal h1-a8.
main.hint: Prepare a home for your king's bishop on the long diagonal.

main.strategic_idea: Set up a solid central anchor and challenge White's expansion.
main.explanation: Black places a pawn firmly in the middle of the board and blocks the long diagonal for now.

main.strategic_idea: Put the bishop on its strongest square.
main.explanation: From g2 the bishop puts long-range pressure on Black's queenside along the h1-a8 diagonal.
main.hint: Develop your bishop onto the long diagonal.

main.strategic_idea: Develop calmly and keep the center closed.
main.explanation: Instead of taking on c4 (the Open Catalan), Black keeps the pawn on d5 and develops the bishop quietly to prepare castling.

main.strategic_idea: Control d4 and e5 and prepare to castle.
main.explanation: The knight develops to its natural square, watches the central squares d4 and e5, and clears the way for castling.
main.hint: Develop your king's knight and get ready to castle.

main.strategic_idea: Make the king safe before the center opens.
main.explanation: Black castles short quickly, before any fight in the center begins.

main.strategic_idea: Secure the king behind the fianchetto and activate the rook.
main.explanation: The king is safe behind the g2-bishop and the pawns, and the h1-rook joins the game.

main.strategic_idea: Build the c6-d5-e6 pawn triangle against the g2-bishop.
main.explanation: This solid pawn triangle absorbs the pressure of the g2-bishop along the long diagonal.

main.strategic_idea: Protect c4, watch the c-file and prepare e2-e4.
main.explanation: The queen defends the c4-pawn, controls the c-file and supports the coming central push e2-e4.
main.hint: Place your queen where it guards c4 and supports e4.

main.strategic_idea: Develop the knight to support d5 and the center.
main.explanation: The knight protects the d5-point and keeps Black's central structure compact.

main.strategic_idea: Develop flexibly to support the central break while keeping c4 protected.
main.explanation: The knight supports e2-e4 from d2 and can recapture on c4 if needed.
main.hint: Develop your queen's knight so it supports e4 and guards c4.

main.strategic_idea: Prepare to fianchetto the light-squared bishop.
main.explanation: Black's light-squared bishop on c8 is shut in by the e6-pawn, so Black prepares ...Bb7 to bring it to the long diagonal a8-h1.

main.strategic_idea: Break open the center to free the g2-bishop.
main.explanation: White strikes in the center to open lines for the pieces and release the g2-bishop along the long diagonal h1-a8.
main.hint: Your pieces are ready: strike in the center.

levels.title: The 6...c6 setup and the e2-e4 break
Test: play the 6...c6 setup from memory
